home-remodeling.local_heading: A master-planned city, thirty years on
intro_paragraphs: Weston came out of a plat book before it came out of the ground. Arvida built it as Indian Trace, renamed it Weston in the mid-1980s, and finished the first houses in Country Isles and Windmill Ranch. The city incorporated in 1996, and Bonaventure voted itself in the next spring. That history is legible in the houses. Emerald Estates and The Ridges are full of 1990s Mediterranean production homes with barrel tile and arched entries, Weston Hills Country Club rings its golf courses with subdivisions, and Windmill Ranch Estates holds custom estates on acre-plus lots. None of it is falling down. Most of it is thirty years past its plan.

Two approvals matter here and only one belongs to government. Nearly every Weston residence sits inside a private development whose architectural review committee sees your elevations before the city does, and those associations register annually with the City Clerk. Permits then run through Weston's Building Code and Permitting Services Department, which enforces the Florida Building Code together with Broward County regulations administered by the Board of Rules and Appeals. Submittals are electronic, digitally signed and sealed, and named to the city's file convention. Impact windows and doors carry High-Velocity Hurricane Zone approvals, because Broward sits in the HVHZ alongside Miami-Dade.

Over 150 delivered remodels and additions and more than twenty years of South Florida building stand behind those promises, all permitted and inspected. On a Weston job that means a fixed written scope before demolition, a supervisor on site each working day, and crews who clear the guard gate on schedule with whatever paperwork the association asked for. Existing floors, cabinetry and pool decks get protected rather than apologized for. One team owns the project from estimate through final inspection and warranty.
home-remodeling.scope_heading: What a full Weston remodel touches
home-remodeling.scope_intro: Nothing gets opened before the scope is written. These five pieces show up in nearly every whole-home project inside Weston's gated communities.

scope_items.name: Opening the 1990s plan
scope_items.desc: Taking out the walls that separated formal living, dining and family rooms, with engineered beams and sealed calculations replacing the load path we remove.

scope_items.name: Mechanicals at thirty years
scope_items.desc: New panels, condensers, duct runs and supply lines, because a house framed in 1995 is now past the service life of most things behind its drywall.

scope_items.name: Retiring the accordion shutters
scope_items.desc: Trading original glazing and folding shutters for impact windows and doors with High-Velocity Hurricane Zone approvals, detailed to satisfy your association's elevation rules.

scope_items.name: Floors, trim and millwork
scope_items.desc: One flooring material carried across the whole plan, built-in millwork, and interior doors scaled to ten-foot ceilings instead of the builder set that came with the house.

scope_items.name: Ceilings and lighting rework
scope_items.desc: Flattening popcorn and tray ceilings, adding blocking for fans and fixtures, and running a lighting layout the original electrician was never asked to imagine.

faqs.q: Does my HOA sign off before the city does?
faqs.a: They are separate approvals, and the sane order is association first. Nearly every Weston residence sits inside a private development with its own architectural review, and those associations register annually with the City Clerk. Interior work usually clears quickly. Anything that reads from the street, a roof, a window profile, a driveway, a paint color, wants elevations and product data. We build the association package and the permit set from one drawing set so the two never disagree.

faqs.q: What does the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals actually do?
faqs.a: It is Broward's code-administration layer, and it is why building departments across the county work from one set of amendments. The Board adopts Broward's amendments to the administrative chapter of the Florida Building Code, certifies building officials and inspectors, hears appeals of a code official's decision, and issues formal interpretations when a code section is genuinely disputed. On a house remodel it runs quietly in the background, and it matters on the day a reviewer and an engineer read one paragraph two ways.

faqs.q: Is a full gut worth it on a house from the nineties?
faqs.a: Usually, if you like the street, because what you buy back is layout and infrastructure rather than square footage. A 1995 Weston house generally has sound bones, a dated plan, and mechanicals at the end of their run. Gutting lets you move walls, replace the panel and the duct work, and put impact glass in every opening at once under one permit, instead of paying mobilization three separate times across the next decade.

faqs.q: What does the schedule really look like?
faqs.a: Design and engineering come first, then association review, then city plan review through the ePermits portal. Small, well-defined scopes can ride Weston's quick permit path, which is built for exactly that. A whole-house set is not one of those. Plan on a few months of drawings and approvals before demolition and several more on site, longer when cabinetry and stone are custom, and add a cycle for every round of corrections. Dates go in writing and we defend them.

faqs.q: Why is your proposal higher than the one next to it?
faqs.a: Usually because it is a different document. Ours is a fixed written scope with named products, allowances tied to real selections, and the behind-the-wall work included rather than discovered in week six. We are a licensed general contractor carrying insurance, permits and daily supervision on every job, Lic. CGC1539072. If price is the only variable, we will say so early and part on good terms. Most of our clients are buying certainty, and certainty has a number.

home-remodeling.cta_sub: Bring the floor plan, the association guidelines and the list you keep adding to. You will get straight answers and a written scope, in English o en español.

kitchen-remodeling.title: Weston FL Kitchen Remodeling | PGX Builders Group
kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Weston kitchen remodeling that gets you off the builder's menu: soffits gone, islands templated late, permits handled. (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.h1: Your kitchen, off the builder's menu
kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: Custom cabinetry, stone counters and layout changes for Weston kitchens built between 1985 and 2005. Permitted through the city, inspected at every stage, and run by one supervisor who is on site every working day.
intro_paragraphs: Weston kitchens fail in remarkably similar ways, because so many were framed by the same builders inside a fifteen-year window. Walk through Savanna, The Falls, Country Isles or The Meadows and the plan repeats: a soffit hanging over the wall cabinets, a peninsula standing where an island belongs, a desk nook nobody has used since laptops arrived, and a pass-through cut into the family room wall. Most of these rooms were refinished once, somewhere around 2006, in granite. What owners want now is the room reorganized, not resurfaced again.

Kitchens pull in plumbing, electrical, mechanical and frequently structure, so the work is permitted through Weston's Building Code and Permitting Services Department and inspected as it goes. Drawings upload to the city ePermits portal, digitally signed and sealed, with file names matching the city convention, since a misnamed file gets a submittal rejected before a reviewer opens it. Florida's new exemption for small residential work is no help here either: electrical, plumbing, mechanical, gas and structural scopes are all carved out of it. Exterior venting or a new window goes to your association as well.

Square cabinets come from a build order nobody rushes. Cabinets are ordered against verified field dimensions, stone is templated after the boxes are set rather than before, and appliances are confirmed by model number before a filler strip is cut. Weston clients get a fixed written scope, one supervisor who is on site daily and answers the phone, and dust containment that treats the rest of the house as the finished work it is. Twenty-plus years of South Florida construction stands behind that.
kitchen-remodeling.scope_intro: Cabinetry and stone set the schedule; the rest is sequencing. Five elements we handle on almost every Weston kitchen.

scope_items.name: Cabinetry off the builder's menu
scope_items.desc: Cabinet packages ordered to verified field dimensions and finished for Florida humidity, running to the ceiling instead of stopping under a soffit nobody ever wanted.

scope_items.name: Soffits, peninsulas and walls
scope_items.desc: Demolishing the soffit, retiring the peninsula, and where a wall carries load, replacing it with an engineered beam under a permitted structural drawing.

scope_items.name: Stone islands, templated late
scope_items.desc: Quartzite, marble or porcelain templated once the cabinets are set, with island framing built for slab weight and any seated overhang carried properly.

scope_items.name: Appliances that move
scope_items.desc: Relocating range, hood, refrigeration and dishwasher to where the plan actually wants them, with new circuits, water lines and exterior venting permitted and inspected.

scope_items.name: Power the panel can carry
scope_items.desc: Dedicated circuits, panel capacity checked before an induction range or double oven is specified, and a layered lighting plan on controls that make sense.

faqs.q: Florida exempted small jobs from permits. Does that cover my kitchen?
faqs.a: No. The exemption that took effect on July 1, 2026 applies to single-family work valued under $7,500, and it specifically carves out electrical, plumbing, mechanical, gas and structural work, plus anything on property inside a flood hazard area. A kitchen touches most of that list on day one. The law also forbids splitting a project into pieces to slip under the threshold, and a building department can still ask you to document that the work qualifies. Wrong hill for a kitchen.

faqs.q: Does the association need to see an interior kitchen?
faqs.a: The room itself, rarely. The logistics, always. Most Weston communities want the contractor registered at the gate, work confined to posted hours, dumpsters and material staging handled a particular way, and vehicles parked where they will not generate a complaint by lunchtime. If your scope adds a hood vent through an exterior wall or enlarges the window over the sink, that becomes an exterior change and goes to architectural review with the rest of the elevations.

faqs.q: How long will we be eating takeout?
faqs.a: Custom cabinetry sets the clock. Quality packages take months to build, so we order early and leave your existing kitchen working while they are fabricated. On-site construction commonly runs a couple of months for a straightforward layout, longer when walls move, gas is added or the panel gets replaced. Before anything is demolished we set up a temporary kitchen somewhere sensible, which is the difference between an inconvenience and a grievance.

faqs.q: Can the wall between the kitchen and family room come out?
faqs.a: Often yes, and never on a hallway guess. In most Weston houses the exterior shell is concrete block while interior partitions are framed, which makes many of them non-bearing, but roof trusses and point loads do not care about probability. We open a small inspection, have an engineer look at what is actually up there, and if the wall carries load we detail a beam, seal the drawing and permit it.

faqs.q: What moves the number most on a Weston kitchen?
faqs.a: Cabinetry first, then stone, then appliances, and after that the items nobody photographs: relocating plumbing, adding circuits, replacing a panel, venting a hood through block. Two kitchens with identical footprints can land far apart depending on whether the layout stays put. We scope after a site visit and quote against a specification rather than a square-foot guess, because a per-foot number tells you nothing about what is behind the wall.

kitchen-remodeling.cta_sub: Send photos and a plan, tell us what the room gets wrong, and we will come measure. Real numbers, in English o en español.

bathroom-remodeling.title: Weston Bathroom Renovation, FL | PGX Builders Group
bathroom-remodeling.meta_description: Weston bath renovations retire the 1990s garden tub, rebuild the shower over a tested membrane and add real storage. (786) 273-2524.
bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: Primary suites, frameless showers and freestanding tubs across Weston, with waterproofing that gets flood-tested before tile is ordered. Fully permitted and inspected, licensed and insured, supervised daily by the people who wrote the scope.
bathroom-remodeling.local_heading: The garden tub era is over
intro_paragraphs: Almost every primary bath built in Weston Hills, The Lakes or The Isles at Weston between 1990 and 2005 is the same room wearing different tile: a soaking tub sunk into a deck beneath a glass block window, a cramped separate shower with a molded pan, a cultured marble top carrying two oval bowls, and a closet-sized compartment for the toilet. It was a sensible plan in 1994. Today the tub deck is the first thing owners in Weston want gone, followed closely by the shower and the storage.

Weston's Building Code and Permitting Services Department permits the work, with plumbing, electrical and mechanical inspections at rough and again at final. Broward building departments work from one set of code amendments administered by the Board of Rules and Appeals, which also certifies the inspectors who show up at your rough-in. Owners in the Bonaventure condominiums and the country club villas have a second calendar to watch: Broward's Building Safety Inspection Program, which the Board administers, starts at 25 years and repeats every ten, and it is the association's obligation rather than any individual owner's.

Tolerances in this room are tighter than anywhere else on the job. We flood-test pans and let them sit, slope to the drain rather than toward it, block walls before heavy glass is ordered, and vent to the outside instead of into an attic. Weston clients get a fixed written scope, daily supervision, protected pathways from the front door to the work zone, and crews who sign in at the gate and leave the street clean. Licensed and insured, Lic. CGC1539072.
bathroom-remodeling.scope_heading: The pieces of a bath rebuild
bathroom-remodeling.scope_intro: From a powder room to a full primary suite, the specification is settled before tile is ordered. The usual components follow.

scope_items.name: Losing the tub deck
scope_items.desc: Demolishing the tiled platform, rerouting the drain and supply, and reclaiming the floor area for a freestanding tub, a wider shower or actual storage.

scope_items.name: Showers rebuilt and tested
scope_items.desc: Sloped pans, bonded membranes flood-tested and held before tile, linear drains where they help, and benches and niches framed rather than carved in later.

scope_items.name: Vanities and real storage
scope_items.desc: Custom vanities sized to the wall instead of the catalog, drawer banks that hold what a bathroom actually holds, and stone tops with undermount bowls.

scope_items.name: Glass block and daylight
scope_items.desc: Replacing dated glass block with impact-rated units or obscured glazing, which changes both the light in the room and the elevation your association reviews.

scope_items.name: Ventilation and moisture control
scope_items.desc: Quiet fans ducted through the roof rather than into the attic, moisture-rated fixtures, and heavy glass hung on solid blocking installed while walls are open.

faqs.q: Our shower has leaked once already. What did the original build get wrong?
faqs.a: In houses of this era the usual suspects are a pan that was never flood-tested, a liner cut short at the curb, backer board run to the floor with no membrane, and an exhaust fan dumping into the attic. None of that is visible from inside the finished room, which is why it announces itself as a stain on the ceiling below. We rebuild the whole assembly and test it before tile is ordered.

faqs.q: Can the garden tub go and the shower take the whole wall?
faqs.a: It is the most requested change we see in Weston primary baths, and it usually works. The deck comes out, drain and supply get rerouted, and the shower runs the length of the old wet zone with a bench, a linear drain and heavy glass. Where a glass block window sits above the old deck we either keep it, swap it for an impact unit, or close it and light the room another way. Only the window concerns your association.

faqs.q: Which parts of a bath remodel actually need a permit?
faqs.a: Anything that moves water, power or air. Relocating a drain, adding circuits, changing the exhaust route or altering framing all get permitted through Weston's Building Code and Permitting Services Department and inspected before they are covered. Swapping a faucet or repainting does not. The inspection sequence is the point: it puts eyes on waterproofing and rough plumbing at the only moment anyone can see them, and it leaves a record a buyer's inspector will look for.

faqs.q: Our building is due for its 25-year inspection. Does that stop our unit remodel?
faqs.a: No, but coordinate. Broward's Building Safety Inspection Program, administered by the county Board of Rules and Appeals, begins at 25 years and recurs every ten, and it produces a structural and electrical safety report signed by an engineer or architect. It runs on the building and belongs to the association. One- and two-family dwellings are exempt, so a detached Weston house never sees it. If your Bonaventure or country club building has repairs pending, we sequence unit work around the association's contractors.

faqs.q: What should a primary bath at this level cost?
faqs.a: Stone, glass, fixtures and tile set most of it. The invisible half, waterproofing, new supply and drain lines, ventilation and blocking, is exactly where a low bid found its savings. We walk the room, scope what the house genuinely needs and put a fixed number against a written specification. We compete on finish quality and on that number holding, not on being cheapest of three, and we would rather say so at the first visit.

bathroom-remodeling.cta_sub: Show us the room and tell us what fails at seven in the morning. You get a scoped, fixed written estimate, in English o en español.

home-additions.title: Home Additions & Extensions, Weston FL | PGX Builders
home-additions.meta_description: Additions inside Weston's gated communities: rear extensions, second stories, in-law suites. Engineered, permitted, supervised daily. (786) 273-2524.
home-additions.h1: Room to grow inside the plat
home-additions.hero_sub: Rear extensions, second stories, patio enclosures and in-law suites for Weston homes, engineered and permitted through the city, cleared with your association first, and built by a licensed general contractor under a fixed written scope.
home-additions.local_heading: Setbacks, easements and the lake behind you
intro_paragraphs: Additions in Weston begin with a survey rather than a sketch, because these lots were platted, not inherited. Homes in Savanna, The Ridges and Country Isles sit on tightly drawn parcels with side setbacks measured in single-digit feet and rear yards that end at a lake bank or a drainage easement. Estates in Windmill Ranch Estates and parts of Weston Hills have genuine room to move. The projects are the same either way: enclose the screened patio, push the family room back, build over the garage, or add a proper suite for a parent.

An addition draws the full review. The association sees elevations first, then the plan set goes to Weston's Building Code and Permitting Services Department, with the city's engineering and planning divisions involved when drainage, driveways or zoning setbacks come into play. Expect sealed structural drawings for footings and tie beams, HVHZ product approvals for every new opening, and a current survey showing easements most owners have never looked at. If a tree stands in the footprint, removal or relocation needs a city landscape permit, and that includes trees on association ground.

A builder's habits become permanent the day an addition is poured. We tie new footings to existing ones the way the engineer drew it, match stucco texture and roof tile so the seam stops announcing itself after a year, and keep the occupied half of the house sealed and livable while the new half goes up. The scope is fixed in writing before the first excavation, the site has a supervisor every working day, and the same team carries the job from feasibility to warranty.
home-additions.scope_intro: Every addition begins with a survey, an engineer and a look at the covenants. These are the five shapes Weston additions usually take.

scope_items.name: Pushing into the platted yard
scope_items.desc: New living space built to the edge of the platted envelope, with footings, beams and the roof joint engineered as one package.

scope_items.name: Second stories over the garage
scope_items.desc: Upper floors added where the existing footings and block walls check out, designed to sit inside the roof language your association already approved once.

scope_items.name: Screened patio to conditioned room
scope_items.desc: Turning the cage into real interior space with impact glazing, insulation, mechanical extensions and a permitted roof, so the square footage counts at appraisal.

scope_items.name: Quarters for long-stay family
scope_items.desc: Independent suites with bath, closet and kitchenette for long-stay family, built to code and detailed to read as original rather than attached.

scope_items.name: Footings, tie beams and trusses
scope_items.desc: Underpinning, new footings, reinforced tie beams and truss modifications: the half of the budget nobody sees and the half that decides whether it lasts.

faqs.q: Can I turn the screened patio into a real room?
faqs.a: Frequently, and it is a genuine addition rather than an upgrade. The existing slab and footings get evaluated for new load, the openings become impact-rated glass and doors with HVHZ approvals, insulation and mechanical extensions come in, and the roof is built for wind uplift. It is permitted as new conditioned area, which is what makes the square footage count at appraisal. Enclosures done without permits tend to surface at closing and cost more to fix than to have done properly.

faqs.q: Will my association approve an addition at all?
faqs.a: Some Weston communities are open to it and some are restrictive, and the covenants answer that before an architect can. Review typically looks at massing, roof pitch and tile, stucco finish, window profiles and how the new volume reads from the street or the lake. We read the governing documents early, design toward them, and bring the association a complete package instead of a sketch. That is usually the difference between one meeting and three.

faqs.q: How close to the lake or the golf course can I build?
faqs.a: Less close than the yard suggests. Weston lots carry platted setbacks plus drainage and lake maintenance easements, and the lakes and drainage inside most of the city are run by the Indian Trace Development District, a dependent district governed by the City Commission itself, so the buildable envelope often stops well short of the bank. A current survey settles it. We map setbacks, easements and utility runs before anyone draws a floor plan, because moving a wall on paper is free and moving a footing is not.

faqs.q: Can a Weston house take a second story?
faqs.a: Many can, with work. A structural engineer evaluates the existing footings, block walls and tie beam, then designs reinforcement, new columns or an upgraded tie beam where the numbers demand it. Sometimes the honest answer is that pushing back into the yard costs less and lives better than going up. We get that engineering done early and hand you real options with numbers attached rather than one plan and a shrug.

faqs.q: How long does an addition take end to end?
faqs.a: Longer than the construction phase implies. Survey, design, structural engineering and association review come first, then city plan review across the building, engineering and planning divisions, each with its own calendar. For a substantial addition, several months of front-end work before ground is broken is normal, with construction running months beyond that. You get the whole sequence in writing at the estimate, including which steps are ours and which belong to the city.

home-additions.cta_heading: Bring the survey, we will bring questions
home-additions.cta_sub: Twenty minutes on site tells us more than a week of guessing. Feasibility, setbacks and an honest range, in English o en español.

outdoor-living.title: Outdoor Living & Patios in Weston, FL | PGX Builders
outdoor-living.meta_description: Weston backyards past the aluminum cage: covered patios, outdoor kitchens, travertine decks. HVHZ engineered, HOA-ready. (786) 273-2524.
outdoor-living.hero_sub: Covered outdoor kitchens, rebuilt screen enclosures, travertine decks and pergolas for Weston backyards. Engineered for High-Velocity Hurricane Zone loads, permitted through the city, and installed by a licensed, insured general contractor.
intro_paragraphs: Weston backyards arrived with a standard kit: a rectangular pool, a broom-finished deck, and an aluminum screen enclosure drawn to the smallest footprint the plan allowed. On the lakefront streets of The Lakes, The Isles at Weston and Windmill Ranch Estates, that cage frames one of the better views in west Broward, which is a peculiar thing to do to a view. So the work here runs one direction: the enclosure comes out or goes up taller, the deck is redone in travertine or large-format porcelain, and a covered outdoor kitchen replaces the grill on wheels.

Exterior work in Weston answers to two desks. The association reviews enclosure height, screen color, deck material, paint and anything legible from the street or the water. The city permits the construction: building permits for structures, pool decks and screen enclosures through Weston's Building Code and Permitting Services Department, engineering permits for driveways and underground drainage, and a landscape permit before any tree is removed or relocated. Covered structures and new openings need High-Velocity Hurricane Zone product approvals and engineered connections, since Broward is HVHZ territory.

Outdoor rooms in South Florida fail from the details inward. We run gas, water and power under permit instead of under the deck, engineer pergola and roof connections for uplift, pitch paving so water leaves the house rather than pooling at the slider, and specify hardware that will not bleed rust down new travertine by the second summer. Fixed written scope, daily supervision, a tidy site, gate paperwork filed before the trucks arrive, and 20-plus years of South Florida construction behind the estimate.
outdoor-living.scope_intro: One coordinated project, one permit set, one crew. These are the exterior elements Weston clients ask for most.

scope_items.name: Covered outdoor kitchens
scope_items.desc: Permitted gas, water and power feeding weather-rated cabinetry and stone, under a roof structure engineered rather than assembled from a catalog photograph.

scope_items.name: Screen enclosures rebuilt
scope_items.desc: Taller, cleaner cage geometry with upgraded screen and hardware, or removal of the enclosure entirely once a compliant pool barrier takes over the job.

scope_items.name: Decks in travertine and porcelain
scope_items.desc: Old pool decks replaced with travertine or large-format porcelain over a base that drains, pitched away from the slider instead of toward it.

scope_items.name: Pergolas engineered for uplift
scope_items.desc: Shade structures with real footings and connections detailed for South Florida wind loads, proportioned to the house rather than to the widest available span.

scope_items.name: Stucco, paint and re-roof coordination
scope_items.desc: Exterior repair, color changes cleared through architectural review, and roofing scheduled alongside the deck work so the yard is torn up once.

faqs.q: Do a pergola and an outdoor kitchen need permits?
faqs.a: Yes, and Weston has made that part relatively painless. Small accessory structures, screen enclosures, pool decks, patios and driveways generally qualify for the city's quick permit path, which is meant to move a complete submittal without a full plan-review queue. Utilities are separate trade permits: the gas, water and electrical serving a summer kitchen get inspected like any other rough-in. Complete is the operative word, and completeness is our job.

faqs.q: Can I remove the screen enclosure and leave the pool open?
faqs.a: You can remove the cage. You cannot remove the barrier. Florida requires an approved pool safety barrier, and if the enclosure was serving as it, something compliant has to take over: fencing with self-closing gates, or approved alarms and covers, permitted and inspected. Plenty of Weston owners trade the cage for a fence and a planted edge and never look back. We scope the barrier as part of the project rather than as a surprise at final inspection.

faqs.q: Who decides the paint color and the deck material?
faqs.a: Your association, in most Weston communities, and it is worth checking before you fall for a slab. Architectural review commonly governs exterior color, roof tile, paver and decking material, enclosure height and screen color, sometimes down to an approved palette. The city permits the construction and reviews the structure. We submit to the association first with samples and specifications, then to the city with the same materials named, so nothing changes between the two.

faqs.q: There is a tree exactly where the patio should go.
faqs.a: Then it needs a permit before it needs a saw. Weston issues tree removal and relocation permits, and that applies to street trees and trees on association property as well as what stands inside your fence. Relocation is often the easier approval, and a mature shade tree in this climate is generally worth designing around. We run the landscape permit alongside the building permit so the schedule does not stall waiting on one oak.

faqs.q: What drives the budget on a backyard project?
faqs.a: Structure and utilities, in that order. A new paver deck is one conversation; a roofed outdoor room with engineered footings, gas, water, power and a finished ceiling is a different one entirely. Appliance and stone selections then move it again. We price from a site visit and a written specification, drainage and under-slab work included, so you are comparing something real instead of a per-square-foot number that ignores everything below grade.

outdoor-living.cta_sub: Walk the yard with us and point at what bothers you. A written scope and a realistic schedule follow, in English o en español.
